One Request, Four Memories: What an Agent Must Remember to Book 'the Same Hotel as Last Time'
The CoALA memory taxonomy (working, episodic, semantic, procedural) made concrete — with the store, the freshness rule, and the failure you get when each one is missing.
"Book the same hotel as last time in
Chicago, under $200, and don't forget my
Knows how to call the booking
scratch notes for the active task.
The context window itself (+ compaction) • ADK
Dies with the task; compact above ~60% of
Agent forgets the $200 limit by turn 12 (context
What happened before: past bookings, past tool
results, past user decisions — with timestamps.
Firestore / PostgreSQL event log • Mem0 or Letta
Keep forever; rank by recency; never rewrite
'Same as last time' has nothing to resolve
Stable facts about the user and the world:
Every fact carries source + timestamp (+ git
SHA for code facts); flag STALE on mismatch.
Books a double; or trusts a policy that changed
How to do things: tool-use recipes, learned
Change only through a reviewed PR + golden
Re-learns the API every session; repeats the same
Store receipts, not vibes: every long-term memory carries where it came from and when — so the agent can tell 'I know this' from 'I knew this once'.
Working memory is free; the other three are design decisions. Decide them before the first user does.
